DRAFT MINUTES
  ADJOURNED PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 8, 2025

1.  CALL TO ORDER

An adjourned meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
called to order by CHAIR OLSON at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

CHAIR OLSON led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Olson, Nicklas, Medawar, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo

  Commissioners Absent:  Repp-Loadsman

  City Staff Present: Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, AUGUST 4, 2025

COMMISSIONER  MEDAWAR  made  a  motion,  seconded  by  COMMISSIONER
SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSIONER MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 4,
  2025.

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR NICKLAS to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

NONE

Commissioner Schachter recused himself from Item No. 8A due to relationship with the
applicant.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-250112; ADDRESS: 22 Sorrel Lane, Rolling Hills
  Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Ryan Carstensen, Charles E. Thomas, Inc.; A
  1
Adjourned Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 8, 2025
   request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-250113) for first-and
  second-story additions to an existing split-level residence, a Variance (V-250114) to
  allow construction within non-conforming east and west side yard setbacks, a
  Variance (V-250115) to legalize an existing non-conforming front yard setback and an
  encroachment into a required front yard that is closer than 25 feet from the front
  property line, a Grading Application (G-250234) for import of more than 20 cubic yards
  of earth materials and fill that is more than three feet in height at its deepest point,
  and a Minor Deviation (MD-250245) for a decrease of less than 10% of the required
  front yard. The application was reviewed in accordance with the California
  Environmental Quality (Public Resources Code §21000 et seq.: “CEQA”) and was
  determined to be Categorically Exempt under Class 3, Section 15303(a) New
  Construction of Small Structures.

Director Naughton presented Planning Application No. PA-250112, which proposes an
approximately 800 sq. ft. first-floor addition, an approximately 1400 sq. ft. second-floor
addition, and a 95 sq. ft. garage expansion with reorientation to face the street. A drafting
error in the original plans showed the garage as too narrow, but revised plans now meet the
required 20-foot width by adjusting the interior wall without altering the exterior. The project
also includes grading with over 20 cubic yards of fill to support a new patio and reduce
massing, as well as replacement of a deteriorating 40-foot retaining wall along the western
property line. Two variances are requested to legalize existing non-conforming setbacks from
the home which was built in 1947 and to allow additions within those setbacks. At the
previously scheduled meeting, the neighbor at 20 Sorrel Lane submitted written concerns
regarding view obstruction, erosion, neighborhood compatibility, and overhanging tree
branches, which led to the postponement of this item. Staff visited that site and observed
that the view obstruction is from the exterior of the home; staff informed the neighbor that
per the City’s code, the view impacts are limited to those observed from the interior of the
home. Staff observed overhanging branches, and the applicant has agreed to trim the tree.
Additionally, staff observed erosion caused by an older retaining wall; the applicant has
agreed to replace this portion of the wall.

Director Naughton stated that staff found that the project is compatible with neighborhood
character and can support the requested variances and minor deviation.

Director Naughton stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open the
public hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues; close the public hearing; and adopt
Resolution No. PA-250112, approving the project.

In response to a question from VICE CHAIR NICKLAS, Director Naughton stated that public
hearings are noticed in the paper, and notices are mailed to properties within a 500’ radius
or the subject property. This application was noticed twice, once for the August agenda and
again for this meeting. Notices are also posted on the city’s website.

CHAIR OLSON asked about the Neighborhood Statistics information. Director Naughton
provided the information which was contained in the findings for Neighborhood Compatibility.

CHAIR OLSON inquired about the existing retaining wall and fence located on the east side
of the property, creating a combined height of 10 to 12 feet at the lower end of the property.
He asked if it is the applicants’ wall or that of the neighbor on the east side. Director Naughton
stated that the wall appears to be on the neighbor’s property and stated that any
modifications or improvements would require the neighbor's authorization. Furthermore,
under current code, fencing is not permitted directly on top of a retaining wall unless there is
a horizontal setback equal to the fence or wall height. However, the height itself is not an
issue for the current project.

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

Ryan Carstensen, Applicant, stated that he was grateful with the planning department’s staff support
through this process and feels that the product presented is compatible and mirrors the aesthetic of
  2
Adjourned Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 8, 2025
 the neighborhood. He stated that the proposed project will be an asset and will add value to the
neighborhood.

CHAIR OLSON stated that the Dapplegray Lanes Property Owners Association (DLPOA)
encouraged the applicant to have the plans reviewed by surrounding neighbors and asked if this was
done. Mr. Carstensen stated that he spoke with members of the DLPOA and spoke with several
neighbors; some neighbors were not home or did not wish to talk. He left the plans and a card for
any feedback. Mr. Carstensen stated that due to current condition of the home, neighbors are looking
forward to a “breath of fresh air”.

Dr. Parducho, 20 Sorrel Lane, stated that she recently purchased this home and it is a beautiful
community. She stated that prior to the August meeting she came to speak with staff about concerns
about the size of the project and how it would impact her property. She stated that she spoke with
staff and the property owner who informed her that they would be trimming the trees. However, her
main concern was with the soil erosion on her side of the property. The applicant agreed to address
her concerns. Director Naughton added that the applicant has included in the plans the portion of the
retaining wall to address the erosion on the neighboring property.

Mr. Alex Grabow, 24 Sorrel Lane, stated that his primary concern is the existing retaining wall which
has a 4 - 5-foot fence on top, situated between two properties. He stated that there is limited access
along the side of the homes, any fence maintenance or replacement might also trigger setback
requirements, which could reduce privacy. He stated that this is an older fence and asked for a
variance to replace the fence since it may be damaged during construction or soon after. He also
stated concerns with grading on the back side of the property where the addition is planned to be
built, since he does not believe the existing retaining wall could sustain the addition and infill from
grading.

Mr. Grabow requested clarity on whether a variance can allow rebuilding the existing fence in the
same location and height. He also suggested formalizing an agreement or condition during the
planning or permit approval process to ensure accountability if the wall is compromised post-
construction. City staff clarified that while a non-conforming structure like the fence can be repaired
(but not enlarged), and drainage/grading plans will be reviewed to avoid adverse impacts, they cannot
guarantee the wall's future condition. A neighborly solution like sharing costs, should damage occur
down the line, was also suggested as a potential path forward.

In response to a question by CHAIR OLSON regarding the retaining wall with the fence on top,
Director Naughton stated that it appears that the retaining wall is already set back at least 2 feet from
the property line and RHEMC Chapter 17.64 governs all the requirements for non-conforming
structures and uses within properties in the city and it does allow for a non-conforming structure to
remain as legal non-conforming, and further allows maintenance, in order for it to remain safe, as
long as there are no enlargements or structural changes.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked who has responsibility to repair the wall if it is damaged during
construction. Director Naughton stated that there are conditions within the building code that require
that construction not adversely impact adjacent properties. She stated that if there were impacts to
off site adjacent properties then these would need to be addressed by the applicant; in absence of
that, if in a year from now when construction is completed, it would be the responsibility of the owner.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI suggested that the parties come to an agreement to add as a
condition of approval to avoid any future conflict. Director Naughton stated that during the building
permit review and issuance process, the applicants will be submitting and creating a drainage plan
to ensure that no drainage would leave the site that could adversely impact surrounding properties.
Additionally, it ensures that any construction activity would not adversely affect adjoining property
owners. She also noted that the building and safety review could consider an existing retaining wall—
located on an adjacent property as shown by survey—and ensure that grading plans account for it.
Specifically, the review will assess whether the fill added to the southeastern portion of the site would
impose excessive load on the off-site retaining wall, integrating this concern into the overall grading
review.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that he recalls a similar situation a few years back where the
neighbors split the cost. It would be the neighborly thing to do, since it's an unknown down the road.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

  3
Adjourned Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 8, 2025
 CHAIR OLSON asked if the recommendations from the DLPOA regarding the construction should
be included as a condition of approval. Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission can
certainly add a condition that all the requirements outlined in the DLPOA correspondence be
incorporated into the proposal. CHAIR OLSON stated that he is satisfied that they have already been
included in the report.

Director Naughton stated that condition #14 was added, stating that an 8-foot wide by 40-foot-long
DG or equivalent surface as shown on Exhibit A outside of the improved asphalt area be provided
for street parking purposes.

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-250112 WITH THE CONDITIONS
  OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT.

Ayes: Olson, Nicklas, Medawar, Romanelli, Yoo
Noes:
Absent: Repp-Loadsman
Abstain: Schachter

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Resolution No. PA-250112, a
resolution of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates granting a Neighborhood
Compatibility Determination for first-and second-story additions to an existing split-level residence, a
Variance to allow construction within non-conforming east and west side yard setbacks, a Variance
to legalize an existing non-conforming front yard setback and an encroachment into a required front
yard that is closer than 25 feet from the front property line, a Grading Application for import of more
than 20 cubic yards of earth materials and fill that is more than three feet in height at its deepest
point, and a Minor Deviation for a decrease of less than 10% of the required front yard. There is a
20-day appeal period by which any member of the public or the Council, by its own motion, may
appeal this project.

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked about the project at 758 Silver Spur Road (Bart Earle Way).
Director Naughton stated that the project was revised and will be coming back before the Planning
Commission at its October meeting.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

Director Naughton announced that the City Celebration is scheduled for Saturday, September 13 at
a new location – Ernie Howlett Park due to an equine sickness.

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, AUGUST 26, 2025

RECEIVED AND FILED.

12.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR OLSON adjourned the meeting at 8:48 p.m. to the next adjourned Planning Commission
meeting on Monday, October 4, 2025, at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos
Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.

Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst  Larry Olson, Chair

  4
Adjourned Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 8, 2025
